$description: UberTib PRIMITIVE space, size, radius, border width, elevation and opacity. Literal values live only in this file. A component never references a primitive; it goes through the semantic layer.

space.$description: 4px base unit. Every value is a multiple of 4 except the two 2px hairline steps.

size.$description: Control heights, interactive target floors and icon sizes.

control-sm.$description: Dense-mode control. Requires an expanded hit area to reach the target floor.

target-minimum.$description: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 floor. No density mode may render an interactive target below this, hit area included.

target-comfortable.$description: v2.1 section 15.4 and the design-kit recommendation. Floor for every Patient primary action.

icon-sm.$description: Inline within dense operational text only.

icon-md.$description: Default. Status icons and control affordances.

icon-lg.$description: Patient primary actions and section headers.

radius.$description: Modest by direction. Nothing is fully rounded except a genuinely circular object.

full.$description: Circular objects only - avatar, dot. Never a pill-shaped status chip: a pill reads as a tag rather than as an authoritative state.

hairline.$description: The default separator in this system. Separation is by hairline and surface, not by shadow.

elevation.$description: Deliberately shallow. Most surfaces are flat. Shadow is reserved for a surface that genuinely floats above the page; it never encodes importance, and it never encodes a lifecycle state.

0.$description: Flat. The default for cards, rows, panels and sections.

1.$description: A surface that is draggable or genuinely detached. Not a resting card.

opacity.$description: Opacity never encodes a lifecycle state and never dims read-only authoritative content. Read-only is a colour and affordance decision, not a transparency one.

hover.$description: Neutral overlay for a hover wash on Profile A. Never emitted on Profile C.

disabled.$description: Non-text affordances of a disabled control only. Disabled text uses its own colour token.
